title: Keyed Column and Row Headings

illustrates.quote: m. Use cell-5 headings to group key items by column and row headings. List keyed column headings first, preceded by “Column headings” as a cell-5 heading. Next, list the keyed row headings preceded by “Row headings” as a cell-5 heading. (See Sample 11-16: Keyed Column and Row Headings on page 11-41.)

print.caption: SAT Scores by Race and Ethnicity
print.printFeatures: Bordered box; centered bold title spanning the full box width above the header row; header row bold; row headings wrap to two lines for the longer category names.

braille.notes: Long column headings ("SAT Verbal Mean Scores", "SAT Math Mean Scores") and row headings ("Native American or Alaskan Native", "African American", "White (excluding Latino origin)") are keyed to short two/three-letter codes per rule 11.8: column keys 'mms' (SAT Math Mean Scores), 'rec' (Racial/Ethnic Category), 'vms' (SAT Verbal Mean Scores); row keys 'nan' (Native American...), 'aam' (African American), 'wht' (White...). The transcriber's note (lines 4-14) groups them under the two required cell-5 headings "Column headings" and "Row headings" (rule 11.8.2.m), listing column keys alphabetically by key word before row keys, per rule 11.8.2.n-o. The table body (lines 16-20) then uses only the short keys as its column/row headings.

resolution: width/box-rule note: line 1's top box rule is intentionally shorter (34 cells) to leave room for a trailing 3-character reference code ending at cell 41, one cell beyond the section's usual 40-cell body width; both runs already transcribed this line correctly verbatim, and braille.width is still recorded as the section's declared 40 (not measured per-line) to stay consistent with every other item.
